instructions: Scenario for Unreal Engine: generate images, video, 3D, materials, audio and skies with Scenario and land them in this Unreal project. Order: scenario_status, scene_summary, list_models, model_schema, estimate_cost, generate (quote_id and approved_cost from the estimate), wait_for_job, prepare_result_application, apply_result_application, then save_changes. Never resend a request whose job is unknown: use recover_local_job. More tools (the kit's worlds, games and films, Prompt Spark, the Scenario library, the Output Log) are in the catalog: unreal_tools_list or unreal_tools_search, then unreal_tool_execute_<lane> or the tool's own name.

tools.name: scenario_status
tools.title: Get Status
tools.description:
Sign-in state, Scenario team and project, plugin and engine versions, permissions in force, and job counts. Call it first.
Returns: { signed_in, ready, auth, workspace: { team, project }, permissions, spending_disabled, active_jobs, unresolved_jobs, plugin_version, engine_version, last_error }.

tools.name: list_models
tools.title: List Models
tools.description:
Scenario models filtered by lane, modality, capability chip or text. The lane's picks come first. At most 40 rows. Use model_schema next for a model's inputs.
Returns: { models: [{ id, name, modality, does, provider, tags, about, replaced_by }], matched, note }.

lane.description: Plugin lane; its picks come first.

modality.description: Output kind: image, video, 3d or audio.

chip.description: Capability as in the web app: Generate, Edit, Upscale, Remove background, Texture...

query.description: Text search on name, provider and description.

source.description: all (default), catalog (Scenario's models) or trained (the team's own).

include_legacy.description: Also list models Scenario has replaced with newer ones. Default false.

tools.name: model_schema
tools.title: Get Model Inputs
tools.description:
A model's parameters: types, defaults, options, limits, which change the price, and file inputs (they take Scenario asset ids).
Returns: { model_id, lane, the parameters, plugin_defaults, unreal_ready_prompt, files }.

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.title: Check Price
tools.description:
Free price check of a model run (a dry run: nothing is charged). generate needs its quote_id and cu_cost_exact. Quotes are single use and last 120 s.
Returns: { quote_id, cu_cost_exact, cu_cost, discount_cu, expires_in_seconds, priced_parameters, warnings, next }.

parameters.description: Values by parameter name (model_schema). Plugin defaults fill the rest.

lane.description: Where results land; inferred from the model when omitted.

tools.name: generate
tools.title: Generate
tools.description:
SPENDS Creative Units. Runs the request priced by estimate_cost. Needs quote_id and approved_cost equal to its cu_cost_exact. Sent once and never retried: when its outcome is unknown, use recover_local_job, never call again.
Returns: { job_id, next }, or { approval_id, state: pending_approval } while the person approves the spend; then wait_for_job.

quote_id.description: quote_id from estimate_cost: single use, valid 120 s.

destination.description: Content folder for the import, for example /Game/Props. Default: the plugin's folder.

lane.description: Where the results land in Unreal: image, 3d, material, environment, audio, video or render. Inferred from the model when omitted.

required: quote_id from estimate_cost: single use, valid 120 s.

tools.name: job_status
tools.title: Get Job Status
tools.description:
State, progress, cost, files and whether they are downloaded and imported, with the next step. Takes job_id or job_ids; an approval_id from a spend waiting for the person works too.
Returns: { jobs: [{ job_id, state, progress, quoted_cu, charged_cu, files: [{ index, asset_id, role, downloaded, imported_objects }], error, next }] }.

job_id.description: Job id from generate, run_workflow or list_local_jobs, or an approval_id.

tools.name: wait_for_job
tools.title: Wait for Job
tools.description:
Waits until a job is finished and its files are downloaded, up to timeout_seconds (default 45, max 160; agent clients often cut calls at 60 s).
Returns: what job_status returns, with still_running and next when it is not done yet.

job_id.description: Job id from generate or run_workflow.

tools.name: list_local_jobs
tools.title: List Local Jobs
tools.description:
This project's jobs, newest first: every request made from this editor by people, agents and scripts. Survives restarts.
Returns: { jobs: [...] }, each as job_status describes it.

state.description: all (default), active, unresolved (outcome unknown) or finished.

tools.name: list_generations
tools.title: List Scenario Jobs
tools.description:
Recent jobs on Scenario for this project, from any tool, marked when they are already in this Unreal project.
Returns: { generations: [{ scenario_job_id, type, status, model_id, workflow_id, assets, charged_cu, created_at, job_id }], note }; job_id is set when the job is in this project.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.title: List Workflows
tools.description:
Ready workflows: the team's own, Scenario's featured ones, or both.
Returns: { workflows: [{ workflow_id, name, about, inputs, source }] }.

tools.name: workflow_schema
tools.title: Get Workflow Inputs
tools.description:
A workflow's inputs, in the same form as model_schema.
Returns: { name, about } and the inputs as model_schema gives a model's parameters.

tools.name: estimate_workflow
tools.title: Check Workflow Price
tools.description:
Free price check of a workflow run (a dry run: nothing is charged). run_workflow needs its quote_id and cu_cost_exact. Quotes are single use and last 120 s.
Returns: { quote_id, cu_cost_exact, cu_cost, expires_in_seconds, warnings, next }.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.title: Run Workflow
tools.description:
SPENDS Creative Units. Runs the workflow priced by estimate_workflow, with its quote_id and approved_cost equal to its cu_cost_exact. Sent once and never retried: when its outcome is unknown, use recover_local_job.
Returns: { job_id, next }, or { approval_id, state: pending_approval } while the person approves the spend.

quote_id.description: quote_id from estimate_workflow: single use, valid 120 s.

destination.description: Content folder for the import, for example /Game/Props. Default: the plugin's folder.

required: quote_id from estimate_workflow: single use, valid 120 s.

tools.name: list_assets
tools.title: List Scenario Assets
tools.description:
Assets in the Scenario project, newest first. Their ids go straight into file fields.
Returns: { assets: [{ asset_id, kind, type, name, size, model_id, prompt, scenario_job_id, job_id }] }.

kind.description: image, video, 3d or audio; default all.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for the next page.

tools.name: search_assets
tools.title: Search Scenario Assets
tools.description:
Text search in the Scenario project's assets. Their ids go straight into file fields.
Returns: { assets: [...] }, each as list_assets describes it.

kind.description: image, video, 3d or audio; default all.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for the next page.

tools.name: list_collections
tools.title: List Scenario Collections
tools.description:
Collections in the Scenario project.
Returns: the collections as Scenario lists them, each with its id and name.

tools.name: estimate_prompt
tools.title: Check Prompt Spark Price
tools.description:
Free price of Prompt Spark: prompt variants written for a target model, optionally from reference images. approve_prompt needs its quote_id and cu_cost_exact.
Returns: { quote_id, cu_cost_exact, cu_cost, expires_in_seconds, next }.

model_id.description: The model the prompt is for.

prompt.description: The idea to write prompts from.

image_ids.description: Scenario asset ids of reference images.

tools.name: approve_prompt
tools.title: Run Prompt Spark
tools.description:
SPENDS Creative Units. Runs the Prompt Spark call priced by estimate_prompt, with its quote_id and approved_cost equal to its cu_cost_exact. Sent once and never retried.
Returns: { job_id, next } for read_prompt_result, or { approval_id, state: pending_approval } while the person approves the spend.

quote_id.description: quote_id from estimate_prompt: single use, valid 120 s.

required: quote_id from estimate_prompt: single use, valid 120 s.

tools.name: read_prompt_result
tools.title: Read Prompt Spark Result
tools.description:
The prompt variants of a Prompt Spark job (this editor session only).
Returns: the prompt variants Scenario wrote.

tools.name: capture_reference
tools.title: Capture Reference
tools.description:
Captures the level viewport to a PNG, or exports actors to a GLB, as a local reference for upload_reference. Writes only under Saved/Scenario.
Returns: { reference_id, kind, file, captured, next }.

source.description: viewport (default): a PNG of the level viewport; actors: a GLB of the actors.

actor_ids.description: Names or labels; default the selection.

tools.name: upload_reference
tools.title: Upload Reference
tools.description:
Uploads a captured reference (reference_id) or a file the person chose in the editor to Scenario. Free.
Returns: { upload_id, state }; poll reference_upload_status for the asset_id.

path.description: Project-relative path of a file the plugin produced or the person chose.

tools.name: reference_upload_status
tools.title: Get Upload Status
tools.description:
State of an upload_reference call.
Returns: { upload_id, state (uploading, imported or failed), progress, asset_id once imported, error }.

tools.name: recover_local_job
tools.title: Recover Local Job
tools.description:
Resolves jobs whose outcome is unknown: "check" matches them against Scenario's job list; "dismiss" hides a finished job. Only the person can mark a request as not sent.
Returns: { job, linked, dismissed, still_unresolved, next }.

action.description: check (default): match it against Scenario's job list; dismiss: hide a finished job.

tools.name: recover_cloud_job
tools.title: Link Scenario Job
tools.description:
Links a Scenario job (scenario_job_id from list_generations) into this project's job list and downloads its files. Free.
Returns: the linked job, as job_status describes it.

lane.description: Where the results land in Unreal: image, 3d, material, environment, audio, video or render. Inferred from the model when omitted.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.title: Cancel Job
tools.description:
Asks Scenario to cancel a queued or running job. Whether CU are refunded is Scenario's decision.
Returns: the job, as job_status describes it.

job_id.description: Job id from generate, run_workflow or list_local_jobs.

tools.name: scene_summary
tools.title: Summarize Level
tools.description:
The open level: World Partition state (only loaded actors are listed there), one file per actor, data layers, selection, viewport camera, actor counts by class, and a page of actors with labels, ids, classes, locations and tags.
Returns: { level, unsaved_changes, world_partition, selection, viewport_camera, actor_counts, actors: [{ label, id, class, location, tags, placed_by_scenario }], actors_matching, next_page, notes }.

class.description: Only actors whose class name contains this.

page.description: Page of the actor list: next_page from the previous call.

tools.name: object_detail
tools.title: Get Actor Details
tools.description:
One actor by id or label: class, transform, bounds, components, meshes and materials per slot, and Scenario provenance.
Returns: { label, id, class, folder, location, rotation, scale, bounds_center, bounds_size, mesh, materials, components, placed_by_scenario, scenario }.

actor_id.description: Actor id or label, from scene_summary.

tools.name: screenshot_viewport
tools.title: Screenshot Viewport
tools.description:
Image of the active level viewport's camera (no gizmos), returned to you, with the world, camera, FOV and size it shows. Pass camera to render another view without moving the person's viewport (also works with no viewport open). frame_check flags all-black, all-white, uniform, clipped or crushed frames; exposure_override says when the viewport's fixed exposure differs from the game's.
Returns: the image, and { captured, file, frame_check, exposure_override }.

camera.description: Optional view: location_m [x, y, z] in meters, then look_at_m [x, y, z] or pitch and yaw in degrees, and fov (default 70).

tools.name: find_assets
tools.title: Find Assets
tools.description:
Content Browser search by folder, class, name and Scenario origin. Reads the asset registry; loads nothing.
Returns: { assets: [{ path, class, from_scenario }], matched }.

tools.name: asset_detail
tools.title: Get Asset Details
tools.description:
One asset: class, size on disk, referencers and dependencies, source file, Scenario provenance, and mesh checks (scale, triangles, bones).
Returns: { path, class, size_on_disk_kb, referenced_by, depends_on, source_file, scenario, checks }.

checks.description: Load meshes to run checks (default true).

tools.name: output_log
tools.title: Read Output Log
tools.description:
Recent warnings and errors from the Output Log (and Scenario and Interchange messages), newest last.
Returns: { lines }.

severity.description: errors, warnings (default, with errors) or all.

since_seconds.description: Only lines from the last this many seconds.

tools.name: prepare_result_application
tools.title: Prepare Result
tools.description:
Describes how a finished job will land: purpose import, place, material, environment, media_plate, mesh_edit or sequencer_audio, with targets. Changes nothing; apply_result_application applies it.
Returns: { application_id, review, next }.

purpose.description: How the result lands: import, place (default), material, environment, media_plate, mesh_edit or sequencer_audio.

actor_ids.description: Targets (material, media_plate, mesh_edit, at_pivot); default the selection.

location.description: [x, y, z] in cm for at_location.

files.description: File indices to import (job_status); default all.

tools.name: apply_result_application
tools.title: Apply Result
tools.description:
Applies a prepared application once, in one undo step. When agent changes are off, the person gets a proposal instead.
Returns: { state, review, next } with what changed and the import checks, or state pending_approval while the person decides.

tools.name: select_objects
tools.title: Select Actors
tools.description:
Selects actors by id or label (replaces the selection unless add is true).
Returns: { selected }.

add.description: Add to the selection instead of replacing it. Default false.

tools.name: save_changes
tools.title: Save Changes
tools.description:
Saves the packages the plugin created or changed this session (and the level, with World Partition actor files, when include_levels is true).
Returns: { ok, saved_files, warnings, error }.

include_levels.description: Also save the open level and its World Partition actor files. Default false.

tools.name: remove_scenario_items
tools.title: Remove Scenario Items
tools.description:
Removes actors the plugin placed (one undo step), and a job's imported assets when nothing references them.
Returns: the actors and assets removed.

actor_ids.description: Ids or labels of actors the plugin placed.

tools.name: execute_python
tools.title: Run Python
tools.description:
Runs Unreal Python in the editor (game thread) inside one undo step. Off unless the person allows it. Output capped at 20,000 characters.
Returns: { ok, output, result }.

tools.name: unreal_api_help
tools.title: Unreal API Help
tools.description:
Reflection help before writing Python: a class (functions and properties) or one member ("StaticMeshActor", "EditorActorSubsystem.SpawnActorFromClass").
Returns: { type, python, parent, about, functions, properties } for a class, or the member's signature and about.

tools.name: build_world
tools.title: Build World
tools.description:
Creates and opens a new walkable level under /Game/Scenario/Worlds: sun, sky light and fog for the time of day (mist for ground fog), a ground, invisible walls around the play area, a player start and the project's third-person game mode. Generate the Scenario assets first or in parallel; pass them here or to dress_world. Fails if the open level has unsaved changes.
Returns: { level, size_m, play_area_m, player_start_m, landmark_spot_m, game_mode, time_of_day, mist, sun, next }.

name.description: World name, also the level name ("Misty Bamboo Temple").

time_of_day.description: day (default), morning, golden, dusk, night or overcast.

size_m.description: Side of the square play area in meters (40 to 600). Default 120: about a minute to walk across.

ground_material.description: Material from a Scenario material result (created_assets path). Tiled in world space.

ground_tile_m.description: Meters per texture tile on the ground. Default 4.

sky.description: Material or panorama texture from a Scenario environment (skybox) result.

game_mode.description: Blueprint game mode path. Default auto: the project's Third Person, First Person or Top Down template game mode.

mist.description: Ground fog from 0 (clear air, default) to 1 (dense). Above 0 the fog is volumetric: light shafts and lantern glow show in it. 0.6 to 0.9 for a misty scene.

tools.name: dress_world
tools.title: Dress World
tools.description:
Lays Scenario 3D results out on a world made by build_world: a landmark at the center (faces the player start), an optional paved path from the player start to it, props with spacing (lining the path, crossing it as gates, or scattered) kept off the path, plus ground material, sky, mist and looping ambient sound. Meshes are scaled to height_m and rest on the ground. With a sky, the sun is aimed from the sun in the panorama when it shows a clear one (the result's sun says which). Call again with replace true to redo the layout.
Returns: { level, size_m, props: [{ actor, mesh, at_m, height_m, yaw, on_path }], placed, asked, warnings, note }.

landmark.description: The hero object at the center: what the player walks to and the film circles.

mesh.description: Static mesh path (or its import folder).

front_yaw.description: Degrees added so the mesh's front faces the player. Default -90: Scenario 3D models (glTF) face +Y. Try 90, 0 or 180 if it faces away.

path.description: A flat paved strip from the player start to the landmark (or the world's center), in a world-aligned material. Props stay off it.

material.description: Material from a Scenario material result (stone, gravel, planks).

tint.description: [r, g, b] 0 to 1, multiplies the color.

props.description: One entry per Scenario mesh. 300 props at most in total.

height_m.description: Height in meters, or [min, max] for variety. Default 1.5.

area.description: path_sides lines both sides of the path, evenly spaced (lanterns, fences). on_path puts gates and arches across the path so the player walks through them (torii): the widest side crosses the path, and a single gate marks the start of the path. Default anywhere.

yaw.description: "random" (default), "face_center" or degrees. on_path sets its own.

front_yaw.description: Degrees added to face_center (default -90, as for the landmark) or to on_path (default 0).

light.description: true, or {temperature_k (2200), intensity_cd (4), radius_m (4.5), height (0.63 of the prop's height)}: a warm point light inside each placed prop (lanterns, braziers). 48 lights at most per world.

sink_m.description: Sinks the prop into the ground (rocks, roots). Default 0.

ground_material.description: Material from a Scenario material result, as in build_world.

ground_tile_m.description: Meters per texture tile on the ground.

ground_tint.description: [r, g, b] 0 to 1, multiplies the ground's color (the ground_material given, or the one already on the ground).

sky.description: Material or panorama texture from a Scenario environment (skybox) result.

mist.description: Ground fog from 0 to 1, as in build_world. Omit to keep the level's.

ambient.description: Sound from a Scenario audio result, looped over the whole world.

time_of_day.description: day, morning, golden, dusk, night or overcast.

seed.description: Change it for another layout. Default 7.

replace.description: Removes the props, their lights and the landmark of the previous call first. Default true. A new path always replaces the old one.

tools.name: make_game
tools.title: Make Game
tools.description:
Turns the open level (a kit world or a dressed template) into a small game: Scenario pickups spread over free floor (they spin and glow), an optional goal (in front of the landmark when there is one), a timer, looping music and a HUD. Winning: collect every pickup, then reach the goal. Uses the plugin's Scenario Pickup, Goal and Game Rules actors, so the game also works in a packaged build.
Returns: { level, title, pickups, pickup_mesh, time_limit_s, music }.

pickups.description: What to collect: a Scenario mesh, how many, their name on the HUD and a pickup sound.

sound.description: Short Scenario sound played on pickup.

goal.description: Omit for a game won by collecting everything.

mesh.description: Optional mesh (portal, shrine, boat). Without it the goal is a glow.

time_limit_s.description: 0: no limit. Default 25 s per pickup plus 30.

win_sound.description: Scenario sound played when the player wins.

lose_sound.description: Scenario sound played when time runs out.

objective.description: One HUD line. Default: "Collect every <name>, then reach the goal."

accent.description: HUD and glow color, [r, g, b] 0 to 1.

replace.description: Removes the previous game's actors first. Default true.

tools.name: dress_template
tools.title: Dress Template
tools.description:
Copies an Epic template level of this project (third_person, platforming, combat, first_person, shooter, horror) to /Game/Scenario/Games and dresses the copy with Scenario assets: floor and block materials (world-aligned), meshes swapped for template ones (boxes, cubes, cylinders) at the same size, decor props on free floor, sky and music. The template's gameplay stays. Fails if the open level has unsaved changes.
Returns: { level, template, materials_replaced, swapped: [{ replace, with, count }], placed, asked }.

name.description: Name of the copy, also the level name.

template.description: A name above or a level path. Default platforming.

floor_material.description: Replaces the grey grid floors and walls.

swaps.description: Template meshes to replace: which shape, and the Scenario mesh that takes its place.

replace.description: boxes (breakable crates in combat), cubes, cylinders, or a mesh path.

props.description: Scenario meshes scattered as decor on free floor.

sky.description: Material or panorama texture from a Scenario environment (skybox) result.

time_of_day.description: day, morning, golden, dusk, night or overcast.

tools.name: make_film
tools.title: Make Film
tools.description:
Builds a short film in the open level as a Level Sequence: cine cameras on smooth moves (aerial, crane_down, orbit, walk, detail, rise) around the landmark, camera cuts, fade in and out, and Scenario music and sound effects. Default: six shots over duration_s. Then render_film.
Returns: { film, sequence, level, duration_s, shots, audio, next }.

name.description: Film name, also the Level Sequence name.

music.description: Scenario music for the whole film.

sfx.description: Scenario sound effects, each at a time in the film.

focus.description: What the film is about: an actor label, or [x, y, z] in meters. Default: the landmark.

shots.description: Shots in order; default six over duration_s.

focus.description: Actor label or [x, y, z] meters for this shot.

seed.description: Change it for other camera paths.

tools.name: render_film
tools.title: Render Film
tools.description:
Renders a film with Movie Render Queue in the editor, then encodes an MP4 with its music when ffmpeg is installed. Returns at once: poll film_status about every 20 seconds. A 24 s film at 720p draft takes a few minutes.
Returns: { film, state, frames, resolution, output_dir, note, next }.

film.description: Film name or sequence path. Default: the newest film.

quality.description: high: 4 temporal samples (smoother, about 4x slower). Default draft.

tools.name: film_status
tools.title: Get Film Status
tools.description:
Where a film render is: rendering (frames_done of frames), encoding, done (mp4 path) or failed (error).
Returns: { film, state, next } with frames_done and frames while rendering, the mp4 path when done, or error.

film.description: Film name or sequence path. Default: the newest film.

tools.name: kit_status
tools.title: Get Kit Status
tools.description:
What the kit made in the open level: kit world or not, size, props and their lights, landmark, path, sky, time of day, mist, pickups, goal, game rules, films. During Play it reports the player character instead (pawn, pawn_at_m); stop Play to read the level again.
Returns: { level, kit_world } and what the kit made there, or the player character during Play.

tools.name: play_level
tools.title: Play Level
tools.description:
Starts (or stops) Play in the editor so the person can walk the level or play the game. Call kit_status a few seconds after starting: it reports the player character once it has spawned.
Returns: { playing, note }.

tools.name: unreal_tools_list
tools.title: List Unreal Tools
tools.description:
Every tool of this editor's Scenario server, including those not in tools/list: the kit's worlds, games and films, Prompt Spark, the Scenario library, the Output Log. Free.
Returns: { tools: [{ name, title, summary, lane (read, write or delete), listed }] }. listed tools can be called directly; get another tool's input schema from unreal_tools_search, then run it with unreal_tool_execute_<lane> or by its name.

tools.name: unreal_tools_search
tools.title: Search Unreal Tools
tools.description:
Finds tools of this editor's Scenario server by keyword and gives their input schemas. Searches tools only: for models use list_models, for project assets find_assets. Free.
Returns: { results: [{ name, title, lane, listed, description, inputSchema, annotations }] }; run a result with unreal_tool_execute_<lane> or by its name.

query.description: Words matched against tool names, titles and descriptions, for example film or prompt.

limit.description: Most tools to return, 1 to 20. Default 8.

tools.name: unreal_tool_execute_read
tools.title: Run Read Tool
tools.description:
Runs one read-only tool from unreal_tools_search by name, with the same permissions as calling it directly. Tools of the write and delete lanes are refused here, with the executor to use.
Returns: the tool's own result.

name.description: Tool name, as unreal_tools_list or unreal_tools_search gives it.

parameters.description: The tool's arguments, matching its inputSchema.

tools.name: unreal_tool_execute_write
tools.title: Run Write Tool
tools.description:
Runs one tool of the write lane by name: it changes the project, or SPENDS Creative Units, with the same permissions and money rules as calling it directly (price first, quote_id and approved_cost; paid calls are sent once). Read and delete tools are refused here.
Returns: the tool's own result.

name.description: Tool name, as unreal_tools_list or unreal_tools_search gives it.

parameters.description: The tool's arguments, matching its inputSchema.

tools.name: unreal_tool_execute_delete
tools.title: Run Delete Tool
tools.description:
Runs one destructive tool by name, such as remove_scenario_items or the kit's world, game and film tools, with the same permissions as calling it directly. Confirm with the person first. Read and write tools are refused here.
Returns: the tool's own result.

name.description: Tool name, as unreal_tools_list or unreal_tools_search gives it.

parameters.description: The tool's arguments, matching its inputSchema.
